overview: Georgia is a country in the South Caucasus, on the eastern shore of the Black Sea. Its capital and largest city is Tbilisi. Georgia became independent from the Soviet Union in 1991. It has its own unique alphabet and one of the oldest winemaking traditions in the world, going back about 8,000 years. Two regions, Abkhazia and South Ossetia, are outside the government's control.

geography.text: The Greater Caucasus mountains form Georgia's northern border with Russia, with some of the highest peaks in the Caucasus, and the Lesser Caucasus rise in the south. Between them lie valleys and lowlands, warm and humid in the west near the Black Sea and drier in the east. Glaciers cover the highest mountains, and many rivers flow down from them.

history.text: Georgia was one of the first kingdoms to adopt Christianity, in the 300s, and its medieval kingdom reached a golden age under Queen Tamar around 1200. The Russian Empire absorbed Georgia in the 1800s. After a short independence from 1918 to 1921 it became part of the Soviet Union, and it became independent again in 1991. A short war with Russia in 2008 left two regions outside its control.

events.title: Queen Tamar
events.text: The reign of Queen Tamar begins a golden age.

events.title: Independence
events.text: Georgia becomes independent from the Soviet Union.

events.title: War with Russia
events.text: A five-day war leaves Abkhazia and South Ossetia under Russian control.

government.text: Georgia is a parliamentary republic. The Parliament chooses the Prime Minister, and the President has a mostly ceremonial role. Georgia became a candidate to join the European Union in 2023, but in 2024 the government paused the process, sparking months of mass protests. Russia controls the breakaway regions of Abkhazia and South Ossetia.

economy.text: Georgia's economy includes tourism, wine, mining, farming and transport routes linking Asia and Europe. Its wine and mineral water, especially from Borjomi, are exported widely.

culture.text: Georgia has one of the oldest winemaking traditions in the world, going back about 8,000 years; wine is made in large clay jars called qvevri, a method listed by UNESCO. Georgian has its own unique alphabet, and polyphonic singing in several voices is also UNESCO heritage. Feasts, called supra, are led by a toastmaster called the tamada.

items.title: Qvevri wine
items.text: Wine fermented in clay jars buried in the ground.

items.title: Georgian alphabet
items.text: Its three scripts are listed by UNESCO as living heritage.

items.title: Supra
items.text: A feast with long, elaborate toasts.

sport.text: Rugby union is very popular, and Georgia is the strongest European team outside the Six Nations. Wrestling, judo and weightlifting have brought Olympic medals, and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia is a football star.

items.title: Rugby
items.text: Georgia has played at every Rugby World Cup since 2003.

items.title: Lasha Talakhadze
items.text: Two-time Olympic weightlifting champion and world record holder.

items.title: Euro 2024
items.text: Georgia's first major tournament, reaching the last 16.

didYouKnow: Georgia has one of the world's oldest winemaking traditions, around 8,000 years.
The Georgian alphabet is one of only a handful of unique scripts still used today.

keyPeople.name: Shota Rustaveli
keyPeople.text: Wrote The Knight in the Panther's Skin in the 1100s.

keyPeople.name: Khvicha Kvaratskhelia
keyPeople.text: Won the Champions League with Paris Saint-Germain in 2025.
